meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'shameful'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to be ashamed') (мне стыдно = I'm ashamed) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Сегодня днём в зале нет особо сложных заказов.
examples.trans: This afternoon there are no particulièrement complicated orders in the dining room.

examples.text: Шеф просил особо внимательно следить за качеством свежих устриц.
examples.trans: The chef asked to watch the quality of the fresh oysters with particular care.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'great'.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'when'.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

examples.text: Когда ты наконец принесёшь горячий соус на раздачу?
examples.trans: When will you finally bring the hot sauce to the pass?

meanings.note: leaders or superiors in an organization

examples.trans: The management signed an important order.

examples.text: Успокойся, начальство просто не знает всей правды.
examples.trans: Calm down, the leadership simply does not know the whole truth.

examples.text: Официанты всегда обсуждают личную жизнь начальства.
examples.trans: Waiters always discuss the management's personal life.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нятливый'). Qualitative adjective formed with the productive suffix '-тельный'/'-ливый'. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('quick-witted, understanding').

examples.trans: It is great when the boss is understanding.

examples.text: Очень здорово, когда у тебя такое понятливое начальство.
examples.trans: It is really great when you have such an understanding boss.

examples.text: Новый стажёр оказался на удивление быстрым и понятливым.
examples.trans: The new intern turned out to be surprisingly quick and sharp.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'волить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'увольнять'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'зволять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to allow'.

examples.text: Позволяешь ты обижать свою девушку или нет?
examples.trans: Do you allow someone to insult your girlfriend or not?
What do you think you are doing?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'зволить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to allow', forming an aspectual pair with 'позволять'.

examples.trans: Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'вольнять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to fire', forming an aspectual pair with 'уволить'.

examples.trans: You're firing me? Are you serious?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Secondary conversational sense ('people') (plural люди, a different word) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'here'.
person who owns a business or property
Secondary conversational sense ('host') (person receiving guests) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The owner of the restaurant came out into the dining room.
The restaurant owner personally greets the guests.
The owner is busy in the kitchen for now.

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to decide', forming an aspectual pair with 'решить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!
examples.trans: Here it is, the phone! Decide for yourselves what to do. Without me!

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Secondary conversational sense ('that's enough!') (хватит!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

examples.text: Хватит спорить из-за пустяков, давайте лучше спокойно работать!
examples.trans: Enough arguing over trifles, let us just work calmly instead!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'воленный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fired, dismissed').

examples.text: Ты не уволена, я просто пошутила.
examples.trans: You are not fired, I was simply joking.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'paper', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('paper, official document') (colloquial) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Here is a document from the prosecutor's office.

examples.text: Вот бумага из прокуратуры. Слушание будет сегодня вечером.
examples.trans: Here is an order from the prosecutor's office. The hearing will be this evening.

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'тверждать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to confirm', paired with 'подтвердить'.

examples.trans: Do you confirm this, Ivan Vasilyevich?

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be, appear'.

examples.text: Я официально являюсь новой владелицей этого заведения.
examples.trans: I am officially the new owner of this establishment.

examples.text: Все повара обязаны являться на утреннюю смену без опозданий.
examples.trans: All cooks are required to report for the morning shift without delay.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'owner' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я являюсь новой владелицей этого ресторана.
examples.trans: I am the new owner of this restaurant.

examples.text: Владелица соседнего кафе пришла к нам на ужин.
examples.trans: The owner of the neighboring cafe came to our place for dinner.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'for now'.
Secondary conversational sense ('while') (as a conjunction: пока я сплю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('bye, see you') (informal goodbye) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ладно, ребята, всем пока, увидимся завтра утром на смене!
examples.trans: All right, guys, bye everyone, see you tomorrow morning on shift!
